# sampling.library: JitteredCellPoint2D

This slice: JitteredCellPoint2D, JitteredGridPoints2D, Points, StratumPoint2D, StratifiedPoints2D, Points, PoissonCellSize, PoissonColumns, PoissonRows, EmptyCellPoint, IsEmptyCell, PoissonCandidate, PoissonSlotFree.

```plato

    // The point of grid cell (i, j): the cell center displaced by `jitter` of a
    // half-cell along each axis, the displacement drawn from the cell's own hash.
    // Jitter zero is a regular grid and jitter one is one uniform point per cell.
    // The offset comes from `noise.library.plato`, so a jittered grid and a
    // Worley noise seeded alike put their features in the same places.
    JitteredCellPoint2D(region: Bounds2D, cellCounts: IntegerVector2, jitter: Number,
        seed: Integer, i: Integer, j: Integer): Point2D
    {
        var o = FeatureOffset2D(seed, i, j, jitter);
        return Point2D(
            region.Min.X + (i.ToNumber + o.X) * (region.Max.X - region.Min.X) / cellCounts.X.ToNumber,
            region.Min.Y + (j.ToNumber + o.Y) * (region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y) / cellCounts.Y.ToNumber);
    }

    // One point per grid cell, in row-major cell order.
    // Precondition: both cell counts are positive.
    JitteredGridPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, cellCounts: IntegerVector2, jitter: Number,
        seed: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => (cellCounts.X * cellCounts.Y).MapRange(n =>
            JitteredCellPoint2D(region, cellCounts, jitter, seed, n % cellCounts.X, n / cellCounts.X));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: JitteredGridPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => JitteredGridPoints2D(self.Region, self.CellCounts, self.JitterAmount, self.Seed);

    // The k-th sample of stratum `s`, counted row-major: uniform within the
    // stratum, its two coordinates from two independent streams of that
    // stratum's hash. Stratifying bounds the variance of a Monte Carlo estimate
    // without correlating the samples, which is why the draw stays uniform inside
    // the cell rather than being pulled toward its center.
    StratumPoint2D(region: Bounds2D, strataCounts: IntegerVector2, seed: Integer,
        s: Integer, k: Integer): Point2D
    {
        var i = s % strataCounts.X;
        var j = s / strataCounts.X;
        var u = SampleUnit(seed, s, k * 2);
        var v = SampleUnit(seed, s, k * 2 + 1);
        return Point2D(
            region.Min.X + (i.ToNumber + u) * (region.Max.X - region.Min.X) / strataCounts.X.ToNumber,
            region.Min.Y + (j.ToNumber + v) * (region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y) / strataCounts.Y.ToNumber);
    }

    // `samplesPerStratum` points in each stratum, strata in row-major order.
    // Precondition: both strata counts are positive.
    StratifiedPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, strataCounts: IntegerVector2,
        samplesPerStratum: Integer, seed: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => (strataCounts.X * strataCounts.Y * samplesPerStratum).MapRange(n =>
            StratumPoint2D(region, strataCounts, seed, n / samplesPerStratum, n % samplesPerStratum));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: StratifiedPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => StratifiedPoints2D(self.Region, self.StrataCounts, self.SamplesPerStratum, self.Seed);

    //==
    // # Poisson-disk sampling over a background grid
    //
    // No two points closer than `radius`, and no room left anywhere for another
    // point that a dart found — a MAXIMAL Poisson-disk set, which is the
    // canonical blue-noise point pattern.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersampling#Poisson_disc
    //
    // The background grid is the whole point. Cells are radius / sqrt(2) across,
    // which is the largest cell that can hold at most one sample, so a cell's
    // accepted point IS its occupancy record and a candidate only has to be
    // compared against the 5x5 block of cells around it: two cells further away
    // in any direction is already more than `radius`. That is what turns naive
    // dart throwing — which measures every dart against every point accepted so
    // far — from quadratic into linear in the cell count.
    //
    // The cells are visited in scan order and each is given up to `attempts`
    // uniform darts, the first one clearing its neighbourhood winning. Only the
    // EARLIER half of a cell's neighbourhood is ever consulted: the later cells
    // are still empty, and they test against this cell when their own turn comes,
    // so every pair is checked exactly once.
    //
    // Two honest caveats. Visiting cells in scan order is not Bridson's
    // active-list front, which grows outward from a starting point; Bridson needs
    // a grid that is WRITTEN to as it fills and an active list with random
    // removal, and this vocabulary's arrays are immutable values, so the front
    // cannot be carried without an affine builder that several backends do not
    // have. And a scan-order sweep leaves a faint directional bias — a point is
    // pushed away from the cells above and to its left but not from those below
    // and to its right. The radial spectrum reading at the end of this file is
    // where that shows up, and it is small next to the difference between this
    // and uniform random points.
    //
    // Cost is the cell count times `attempts`, so `radius` must be a real
    // fraction of the region: halving it quadruples the work.

    // The background grid's cell size: radius / sqrt(2), the largest cell whose
    // diagonal is still shorter than the radius, so a cell holds one point at most.
    PoissonCellSize(radius: Number): Number
        => radius / Number.SqrtTwo;

    // The number of background-grid columns covering the region, or zero when the
    // radius is not positive — which is the empty answer rather than an error.
    PoissonColumns(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number): Integer
        => radius <= 0.0
            ? 0
            : ((region.Max.X - region.Min.X) / PoissonCellSize(radius)).Ceiling.ToInteger.Max(0);

    // The number of background-grid rows covering the region.
    PoissonRows(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number): Integer
        => radius <= 0.0
            ? 0
            : ((region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y) / PoissonCellSize(radius)).Ceiling.ToInteger.Max(0);

    // The point standing for an EMPTY cell: four radii outside the region's
    // minimum corner, so it is further than `radius` from every point of the
    // region and can never block a candidate. A sentinel and not a validity
    // record because the grid rows below are plain point arrays and nothing
    // outside this section ever sees one.
    EmptyCellPoint(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number): Point2D
        => Point2D(region.Min.X - 4.0 * radius, region.Min.Y - 4.0 * radius);

    // True when a grid slot holds the empty sentinel rather than an accepted point.
    IsEmptyCell(p: Point2D, region: Bounds2D, radius: Number): Boolean
        => p.X < region.Min.X - 2.0 * radius;

    // Attempt `a`'s dart for cell (i, j): a uniform point of that cell, both
    // coordinates drawn from one hash of the seed, the cell and the attempt.
    PoissonCandidate(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number, seed: Integer,
        i: Integer, j: Integer, a: Integer): Point2D
    {
        var cell = PoissonCellSize(radius);
        var h = LatticeHash(seed, i, j, a);
        return Point2D(region.Min.X + (i.ToNumber + HashToUnit(h)) * cell,
                       region.Min.Y + (j.ToNumber + HashToUnit(NoiseMix(h))) * cell);
    }

    // True when `p` clears slot `c` of a grid row: an empty slot never blocks, and
    // an occupied one blocks only inside the radius.
    PoissonSlotFree(p: Point2D, region: Bounds2D, radius: Number,
        slots: Array<Point2D>, c: Integer): Boolean
        => IsEmptyCell(slots[c], region, radius) || slots[c].Distance(p) >= radius;
```
